headline: A Wisconsin power-line setback could push back full power for Oracle's 1.3-gigawatt data center campus to late 2028, a research firm estimates.
score_reason: Pool 5 lowered by 1: the regulator's vote is from 7 Aug 2026 and the Aterio report from 30 Sep 2026, so little is new today.
importance_line: Oracle's customers and Port Washington-area residents are affected, but the dates are one research firm's estimates and the review of the refiled application has not yet begun.
summary: Startup Fortune reports that Wisconsin's Public Service Commission voted unanimously on 7 Aug 2026 to revoke its earlier approval of American Transmission Co.'s application for the power line serving Oracle's 1.3-gigawatt Port Washington data center campus, after the company filed 564 amendments, which Startup Fortune calls a first in the regulator's 95-year history. Research firm Aterio estimated on 30 Sep that full power would arrive around October 2028 in its base case, after Oracle's promised second half of 2027.
notes: A pool item of 4 Oct (Gas Pipeline for Proposed Oracle Data Center Delayed to 2027) may concern the same project; not verified.
